1.explanation:
1. packages/react/src/components/Dropdown/Dropdown.js: this is where the <label> and <div class="bx--form__helper-text"> are rendered. The disabled class color token and helper-text classes here need to be updated to meet contrast, and the rendering of invalidText needs the proper class/token too.  
2. packages/react/src/components/ListBox/ListBoxField.js: getButtonProps from Downshift injects an aria-label of "Open menu" (or "Close menu") which overrides the <ListBox.Field aria-labelledby> you pass in Dropdown. Removing or adjusting that aria-label logic (or deferring to aria-labelledby) will resolve the accessible-name mismatch.  
3. Snapshot files (Dropdown-test.js.snap and ListBoxField-test.js.snap): after you change markup (class names, ARIA attributes) for both contrast and label behavior, the snapshots must be updated to reflect the new output.  

By updating the Dropdown markup and the ListBoxField ARIA logic, and then regenerating the snapshots, all three DAP violations will be addressed.
1.bug_scenario:
When you render the Carbon-react Dropdown component with a titleText, helperText, disabled or invalid state and run IBM DAP, you see three distinct violations:

1. Contrast failures on the disabled label (“This is not a dropdown title.”) and disabled helper text (“This is not some helper text.”) because the disabled color tokens do not meet WCAG AA.
2. Accessible‐name mismatch on the dropdown toggle: visually the control shows “Dropdown menu options,” but the button’s aria-label is hard‐coded to “Open menu,” so DAP flags “Accessible name must match or contain the visible label text.”
3. Contrast failures on the invalidText (“A valid value is required.”) when invalid=true — its token also falls below AA.

All of these originate from how the Dropdown component (and its underlying ListBoxField) assign colors, classes, and ARIA attributes.

2.explanation:
Both of the failures trace back to how the React Dropdown composes its label, helper text, and button:  

• Dropdown.js (packages/react/src/components/Dropdown/Dropdown.js) is rendering the form label (<label>…</label>) and helper (<div className=‘bx--form__helper-text’>…), toggling “--disabled” classes via Carbon CSS, and then binding aria-label or aria-labelledby on the inner ListBox.Field to the titleText id. That results in:  
  – A low-contrast “--disabled” label/helper style that fails WCAG AA  
  – aria-label/aria-labelledby pointing at the developer-supplied titleText (“This is not a dropdown title”) while the visible button text is the placeholder label (“Dropdown menu options”), causing an accessible name mismatch.  

• ListBoxField.js (packages/react/src/components/ListBox/ListBoxField.js) is where the aria attributes (aria-label, aria-labelledby, aria-expanded, etc.) get assigned on the <div role="button">. It currently picks up aria-label from Downshift’s getButtonProps or the titleText anchor, but it doesn’t align the accessible name with the visible label span. Adjusting it to either:  
  – Remove the hard-coded aria-label so that aria-labelledby (pointing at the visible span) is used, or  
  – Change the aria-label to include/reflect the visible text,  

will resolve the WCAG naming violation.  

Together, these are the two primary files to update: one to fix how the label/helper are rendered in disabled/invalid states so they use a high-contrast color, and one to fix the mismatch between the accessible name and the visible button label.
2.bug_scenario: When you render the Carbon React Dropdown and run IBM DAP against it you see three violations: 1) The disabled title and helper-text are rendered with a very low-contrast color (ratio ~1.7:1) because the “--disabled” variant of the label and helper are too light, and fail WCAG AA. 2) When you inspect the list-box toggle (the <div role="button" …>) its accessible name (computed via aria-label or aria-labelledby) does not match the visible text inside the button (the placeholder/label prop), so DAP reports “Accessible name must match or contain the visible label text.” 3) In the invalid state the same contrast failures recur on the error message text. All of these render flows originate from the React Dropdown wrapper and its use of FormLabel/helper text and the ListBoxField component.
